title: Phish brought near-record crowds to this Fenway dispensary — but not a product shortage
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: New Dia Fenway dispensary in Boston saw near-record sales during Phish concerts at Fenway Park.
The dispensary hosted the Phish Phan Art event, benefitting the Mockingbird Foundation, without facing inventory shortages.
New Dia Fenway plans around major events, maintaining stock for large crowds, including those from international visitors.

title: Red Sox homer 3 times over 7 pitches en route to statement sweep of Dodgers
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox hit three home runs over seven pitches in the third inning against the Dodgers, leading to an 8-4 win.
The victory completed a three-game sweep of the Dodgers, with the Red Sox now holding a 60-51 record.
Boston has won 28 of their last 33 games, securing the second AL Wild Card spot ahead of the trade deadline.

title: Rafaela homers for 3rd straight game as the Red Sox beat the Dodgers 8-4 for 3-game sweep
author: The Associated Press
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela hit a home run in his third consecutive game as the Red Sox defeated the Dodgers 8-4.
Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu hit back-to-back home runs against Dodgers pitcher Emmet Sheehan in the third inning.
Boston Red Sox now have a 23-3 record since July 3, following their sweep of the Dodgers series.

title: Stoughton police chief and town manager placed on leave amid investigation after chief alleges discrimination, harrassment
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Stoughton Police Chief Donna McNamara and Town Manager Thomas Calter placed on paid leave amid discrimination investigation.
McNamara filed a lawsuit alleging Calter's harassment and interference with her role as police chief.
The Stoughton Select Board hired independent investigators for the claims by McNamara and counterclaims by Calter.

title: Here’s what meteorologists are saying about heavy rain and possible flooding Monday
author: Jack Pickell
bullets: The National Weather Service warns of thunderstorms and heavy rain causing urban and poor drainage flooding starting overnight into Monday.
Boston meteorologists foresee high flood risks in urban and poorly drained areas due to expected heavy rainfall Monday.
Meteorologists predict extreme atmospheric moisture will heighten the risk of flooding Monday morning in the Boston area.

title: Review & setlist: Phish soars over Fenway for two nights of rarities and redefined favorites
author: Perry Eaton
bullets: Phish entertained fans at Fenway Park with two nights of unexpected performances and rarities on July 31 and August 1, 2026.
Friday's setlist included a near-18-minute rendition of 'Carini' and a rare cover of XTC's 'Melt The Guns.'
Saturday featured extended jams like an 18-minute 'Ruby Waves' and a set-closing 'Tweezer Reprise' for an energetic finale.

title: Former Patriots 2024 2nd-round pick abruptly retires from NFL
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Ja'Lynn Polk, drafted by the Patriots in 2024, retired from the NFL after two seasons, at age 24.
Polk played just one season with the Patriots, recording 12 catches for 87 yards and two touchdowns.
Polk was traded to the Saints in 2025 but did not play due to injury and has now retired.

title: Mother of trooper killed in crash sues Saugus restaurant, alleging it over-served wrong-way driver
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Barbara Trainor filed a $20 million lawsuit against Tribu Mexican Kitchen & Bar for allegedly over-serving alcohol to Hernan Ramon Marrero.
Hernan Ramon Marrero had a blood alcohol level of 0.192 after consuming nine drinks before the crash that killed Trooper Kevin Trainor.
The lawsuit alleges Tribu continued serving Marrero despite his visible intoxication and failed to prevent him from driving.

title: Red Sox trade deadline live updates: Will Craig Breslow make another big move?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox are actively seeking another impact bat before the MLB trade deadline ends at 6 p.m. Monday.
Boston acquired Curtis Mead from the Nationals, but he fractured his wrist, making another trade likely.
Red Sox are linked with CJ Abrams, but acquiring him requires a hefty package including top prospect Franklin Arias.

title: Man killed in East Boston overnight shooting
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A man was fatally shot near 464 Meridian St., East Boston, around 1:30 a.m. on Sunday.
The victim was pronounced dead at a local hospital; his identity is pending autopsy and family notification.
No arrests have been made; BPD Homicide Unit is investigating and seeking public assistance via 617-343-4470.
